scope: Proposition 2.6 (The deterministic labeled tower) of the manuscript “A torsion-free counterexample to reduced Baum–Connes injectivity” (preprints/A-Torsion-Free-Counterexample-to-Reduced-Baum-Connes-Injectivity-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 285 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 df8d9301aa6d0306), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 15. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For every fixed finite type set and every sufficiently large s as above, the construction has the following properties. 1. The auxiliary state sizes are (2.4). In a fixed extra slice an incidence has degrees d, D. Without slicing, its smaller side acquires the extra factor 2b and its larger side does not. The total degrees are at most T2bd on A and T2bD on B. 2. The labeling is folded: no two outgoing oriented edges at a vertex have the same label. Its signed alphabet satisfies |S| ≤ 2TM2b d2r , p |S| q ≤ 2−.000025s+O(log s)+OT,b(1) −→ 0. (2.20) 3. At every height the fraction of removed vertices on each side is at most εgate +εsep. This bound can be made arbitrarily small, uniformly over heights and all table choices. The separate-parity and terminal gate conclusions of Lemma 2.3 hold. 4. Every immersed path in Xgood starting at height i and having length at least ⌈1.002mi⌉ is the unique immersed path with that oriented word anywhere in Xgood. This is a global assertion over all heights and components.
